title: Comparing how quickly countries are changing their electricity
text: app’s first view follows coal Australia 2005 2025, compared United Kingdom, Germany, United States, China India. share_change() produces numbers: Coal’s share Australia’s electricity fell 36.6 points, largest fall countries, 2025 coal still supplied 42.7% electricity. United Kingdom’s share fell similar amount lower start, almost nothing, India’s share rose. result column text app shows headline table: app’s chart shows comparison:  read : line one country. dots mark start end years. vertical gap country’s two dots change percentage points. steeper line means faster change. focus country blue; countries compared grey.
code: countries <- c(   "Australia", "United Kingdom", "Germany", "United States", "China", "India" )  changes <- share_change(electricity_mix, from = 2005, to = 2025)  coal <- changes |>   filter(source == "coal", country %in% countries) |>   arrange(change)  coal |>   select(country, from_share, to_share, change, change_per_year) #> # A tibble: 6 × 5 #>   country        from_share to_share change change_per_year #>   <chr>               <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>           <dbl> #> 1 Australia            79.3   42.7   -36.6           -1.83  #> 2 United Kingdom       33.8    0.113 -33.7           -1.68  #> 3 United States        49.9   16.3   -33.6           -1.68  #> 4 Germany              47.0   20.6   -26.4           -1.32  #> 5 China                79.2   54.3   -24.9           -1.24  #> 6 India                67.9   70.8     2.90           0.145 coal$result[coal$country == "Australia"] #> [1] "got 42.7% of its electricity from coal in 2025, down from 79.3% in 2005" plot_data <- electricity_mix |>   filter(     source == "coal",     country %in% countries,     between(year, 2005, 2025)   ) |>   mutate(focus = if_else(country == "Australia", "Focus", "Context"))  endpoints <- plot_data |>   group_by(country) |>   slice_max(year, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>   ungroup()  ends <- plot_data |>   filter(year %in% c(2005, 2025))  ggplot(plot_data, aes(year, share, group = country)) +   geom_line(colour = brand[["muted"]], linewidth = 0.75) +   geom_line(     data = filter(plot_data, focus == "Focus"),     colour = brand[["accent"]],     linewidth = 1.5   ) +   geom_point(data = ends, aes(colour = focus), size = 3) +   ggrepel::geom_text_repel(     data = endpoints,     aes(label = country, colour = focus),     direction = "y",     hjust = 0,     nudge_x = 0.4,     segment.colour = NA,     seed = 5523   ) +   scale_colour_manual(values = line_colours, guide = "none") +   scale_x_continuous(     breaks = scales::breaks_width(5),     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.22))   ) +   scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1)) +   coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +   labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of electricity from coal") +   theme_cwd(base_size = 13)

title: Comparing how quickly countries are changing their electricity

code: mix <- changes |>   filter(country == "Australia", !is.na(change)) |>   arrange(change) |>   mutate(     source = factor(source, levels = source),     focus = if_else(source == "coal", "Focus", "Context")   )  ggplot(mix, aes(change, source, fill = focus)) +   geom_col(width = 0.72) +   geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = brand[["ink"]]) +   geom_text(     aes(       label = round(change, 1),       hjust = if_else(change < 0, 1.15, -0.15)     ),     colour = brand[["ink"]]   ) +   scale_fill_manual(values = focus_colours, guide = "none") +   scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.15)) +   coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +   labs(     x = "Change in share of electricity, 2005 to 2025 (percentage points)",     y = NULL   ) +   theme_cwd(base_size = 13)
